prompt: A fish tank is $60$ cm long, $30$ cm wide, and $40$ cm tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?

hint: A fish tank is shaped like a box. Its volume comes from multiplying its three measurements together.

hints.text: A fish tank is shaped like a box. Its volume comes from multiplying its three measurements together.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: A $6 \times 3 \times 4$ box has volume $72$. Your tank is $10\times$ bigger in every direction.
Multiply $60 \times 30 \times 40$. Do $60 \times 30 = 1800$ first, and then multiply that result by $40$.
$1800 \times 40 = 72{,}000$, so the tank's volume is $72{,}000$ cubic centimeters.

explanation: The tank is a rectangular box, so its volume is length times width times height: $60 \times 30 \times 40$.
Multiply the length and width to get the area of the bottom: $60 \times 30 = 1800$.
Multiply by the height: $1800 \times 40 = 72{,}000$, so the volume is $72{,}000$ cubic centimeters.

alternativeExplanations.title: Scale up a small box
steps: Each edge is $10\times$ longer, so the volume is $10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1000\times$ bigger: $72 \times 1000 = 72{,}000$.
